You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# LZ4 - Extremely fast compression

LZ4 is lossless compression algorithm,
providing compression speed > 500 MB/s per core,
scalable with multi-cores CPU.
It features an extremely fast decoder,
with speed in multiple GB/s per core,
typically reaching RAM speed limits on multi-core systems.

Speed can be tuned dynamically, selecting an "acceleration" factor
which trades compression ratio for faster speed.
On the other end, a high compression derivative, LZ4_HC, is also provided,
trading CPU time for improved compression ratio.
All versions feature the same decompression speed.

LZ4 is also compatible with dictionary compression,
which can dramatically improve compression performance on small files.

## Command Line Usage

The `lz4` command line tool provides file compression and decompression:

### Basic Usage

```bash
lz4 [OPTIONS] [-|INPUT-FILE] <OUTPUT-FILE>
```

- `lz4 file1 file2` - compress file1 into file2
- `lz4 -d file.lz4` - decompress file.lz4
- `lz4 -z file` - force compression (creates file.lz4)
- `lz4cat file.lz4` - decompress to stdout (equivalent to `lz4 -dcfm`)
- `unlz4` - equivalent to `lz4 -d`

### Key Options

- `-z`, `--compress` - Force compression
- `-d`, `--decompress` - Decompress
- `-t`, `--test` - Test compressed file integrity
- `-c` - Force write to stdout
- `-m` - Multiple files mode
- `-r` - Recursive mode (directories)
- `-B#` - Block size (4=64KB, 5=256KB, 6=1MB, 7=4MB)
- `-#` - Compression level (1-9 for standard, 10-12 for HC)
- `--rm` - Remove source files after successful compression/decompression
- `-k`, `--keep` - Keep source files (default)
- `-f`, `--force` - Overwrite output without prompting
- `-q`, `--quiet` - Suppress warnings

### Examples

```bash
# Compress a file
lz4 myfile myfile.lz4

# Decompress a file
lz4 -d myfile.lz4 myfile

# Compress multiple files
lz4 -m file1 file2 file3

# High compression mode
lz4 -9 myfile myfile.lz4

# Test file integrity
lz4 -t myfile.lz4
```

### File Format

LZ4 uses the `.lz4` file extension. Multiple `.lz4` files can be concatenated
and will decompress as a single stream.

### Performance Characteristics

- **Compression speed**: Typically > 500 MB/s per core
- **Decompression speed**: Multiple GB/s per core (often RAM-bound)
- **Compression ratio**: Moderate (focuses on speed over ratio)
- **LZ4_HC mode**: Better compression ratio at the cost of compression speed

### Notes

- By default, source files are preserved after compression/decompression
- When input is stdin or output is stdout, data is streamed
- The tool automatically detects `.lz4` files and defaults to decompression
- Use `-q` to suppress progress indicators when scripting

## License

LZ4 is provided as open-source software using BSD 2-Clause license.
---
This repository uses 2 different licenses :
- all files in the `lib` directory use a BSD 2-Clause license
- all other files use a GPL-2.0-or-later license, unless explicitly stated otherwise

Relevant license is reminded at the top of each source file,
and with presence of COPYING or LICENSE file in associated directories.

This model is selected to emphasize that
files in the `lib` directory are designed to be included into 3rd party applications,
while all other files, in `programs`, `tests` or `examples`,
are intended to be used "as is", as part of their intended scenarios,
with no intention to support 3rd party integration use cases.

 -BX    : enable block checksum (default:disabled) 
--no-frame-crc : disable stream checksum (default:enabled) 
--content-size : compressed frame includes original size (default:not present)
--list FILE : lists information about .lz4 files (useful for files compressed with --content-size flag)
--[no-]sparse  : sparse mode (default:enabled on file, disabled on stdout)
--favor-decSpeed: compressed files decompress faster, but are less compressed 
--fast[=#]: switch to ultra fast compression level (default: 1)
--best  : same as -12
Benchmark arguments : 
 -b#    : benchmark file(s), using # compression level (default : 1) 
 -e#    : test all compression levels from -bX to # (default : 1)

Which values can [output] have ? 
---------------------------------
[output] : a filename 
          'stdout', or '-' for standard output (pipe mode)
          'null' to discard output (test mode) 
[output] can be left empty. In this case, it receives the following value :
          - if stdout is not the console, then [output] = stdout 
          - if stdout is console : 
               + for compression, output to filename.lz4 
               + for decompression, output to filename without '.lz4'
                    > if input filename has no '.lz4' extension : error 

Compression levels : 
---------------------
-0  => Default level, identical to -1 
-1  => Fast compression 
-2 .. -12 => High compression; higher number == more compression but slower
--best    => Highest available compression level (-12) 
--fast=#  => Faster compression; higher number == faster but compress less

stdin, stdout and the console : 
--------------------------------
To protect the console from binary flooding (bad argument mistake)
executable will refuse to read from console, or write to console 
except if '-c' command is specified, to force output to console 

Simple example :
----------------
1 : compress 'filename' fast, using default output name 'filename.lz4'
          executable filename

Short arguments can be aggregated. For example :
----------------------------------
2 : compress 'filename' in high compression mode, overwrite output if exists
          executable -9 -f filename 
    is equivalent to :
          executable -9f filename 

executable can be used in 'pure pipe mode'. For example :
-------------------------------------
3 : compress data stream from 'generator', send result to 'consumer'

import sys,struct

        blocks=[]
        while True:
            bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[q:q+4])[0]; q+=4

import sys,struct
# extract raw blocks from an lz4 frame file, print concatenated raw block data (only first block by default)
d=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()
p=0
magic=struct.unpack('<I',d[p:p+4])[0]
assert magic==0x184D2204
flg=d[p+4]; bd=d[p+5]
q=p+6
if flg&0x08: q+=8
if flg&0x01: q+=4
q+=1
out=[]
while True:
    bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[q:q+4])[0]; q+=4
    if bs==0: break
    unc = bs>>31; bs &= 0x7fffffff
    out.append(d[q:q+bs])
    q+=bs
    if flg&0x10: q+=4
sys.stdout.buffer.write(b''.join(out))
EOF
echo ok"}

alphabet=bytes(range(0x20,0x7f))
def rnd(n): return bytes(random.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
exe=sys.argv[1]; level=sys.argv[2]; dsize=int(sys.argv[3]); n=int(sys.argv[4]); positions=[int(x) for x in sys.argv[5].split(',')]
random.seed(42)
dict_ = rnd(dsize)
open('/tmp/t/pdict.bin','wb').write(dict_)
res=[]
for P in positions:
    data = b"\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05" + b"X" + dict_[P:P+n] + b"Y" + b"\x07"*20 + b"z"*300
    qp = 6
    open('/tmp/t/probe15.bin','wb').write(data)
    out=subprocess.run([exe,'-q','-'+level,'-D','/tmp/t/pdict.bin','-c','/tmp/t/probe15.bin'],capture_output=True).stdout
    d=out; flg=d[4]; q=6
    if flg&0x08: q+=8
    if flg&0x01: q+=4
    q+=1
    bs=struct.unpack('<I',d[q:q+4])[0]; q+=4; unc=bs>>31; bs&=0x7fffffff
    blk=d[q:q+bs]
    found={}
    if not unc:
        for s in parse(blk):
            if s[2] is not None:
                mpos=s[0]+s[1]; src=mpos-s[2]
                found[mpos]=(src, s[3])
    r=found.get(qp)
    res.append("%d:%d%s" % (P%3, P, ("Y" if r[0]+dsize==P else "?%d"%(r[0]+dsize)) if r else "-"))
print(' '.join(res))
EOF

content.text: Now let me build a comparison test harness that runs both binaries on many scenarios and compares stdout/stderr/exit codes.

output.arguments:
{"command":"mkdir -p /tmp/cmp && cat > /tmp/cmp/cmp.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: cmp.sh "<args>" [stdin-file]
# runs both binaries in separate temp dirs (copies of /tmp/cmp/data) and compares outputs
REF=/workspace/executable.ref
MY=/workspace/executable
args="$1"; stdin="${2:-/dev/null}"
rm -rf /tmp/cmp/A /tmp/cmp/B; cp -r /tmp/cmp/data /tmp/cmp/A; cp -r /tmp/cmp/data /tmp/cmp/B
(cd /tmp/cmp/A && eval "$REF $args" < "$stdin" > ../A.out 2> ../A.err; echo $? > ../A.rc)
(cd /tmp/cmp/B && eval "$MY $args" < "$stdin" > ../B.out 2> ../B.err; echo $? > ../B.rc)
ok=1
cmp -s /tmp/cmp/A.out /tmp/cmp/B.out || { ok=0; echo "STDOUT differs"; }
cmp -s /tmp/cmp/A.rc /tmp/cmp/B.rc || { ok=0; echo "RC differs: ref=$(cat /tmp/cmp/A.rc) my=$(cat /tmp/cmp/B.rc)"; }
# stderr: compare after stripping timing-dependent parts
python3 - <<'PY' || ok=0
import re,sys
a=open('/tmp/cmp/A.err','rb').read(); b=open('/tmp/cmp/B.err','rb').read()
def norm(x):
    x=re.sub(rb'Done in [0-9.]+ s ==> [0-9.]+ MiB/s  \(cpu load : [0-9]+%\)\n', b'Done in X\n', x)
    x=re.sub(rb'\rRead : \d+ MiB   ==> [0-9.a-z]+%   \r', b'\rRead...\r', x)
    x=re.sub(rb'\rDecompressed : \d+ MiB  ', b'\rDecompressed...', x)
    return x
if norm(a)!=norm(b):
    print("STDERR differs:\n ref:", repr(a[:600]), "\n my :", repr(b[:600])); sys.exit(1)
PY
# compare resulting directory trees
diff -r /tmp/cmp/A /tmp/cmp/B > /tmp/cmp/dirdiff.txt || { ok=0; echo "DIR differs:"; head -5 /tmp/cmp/dirdiff.txt; }
# compare file modes/mtimes
(cd /tmp/cmp/A && find . -type f -printf '%p %m %T@\n' | sort) > /tmp/cmp/A.ls
(cd /tmp/cmp/B && find . -type f -printf '%p %m %T@\n' | sort) > /tmp/cmp/B.ls
cmp -s /tmp/cmp/A.ls /tmp/cmp/B.ls || { ok=0; echo "FILE ATTRS differ"; diff /tmp/cmp/A.ls /tmp/cmp/B.ls | head -4; }
if [ $ok = 1 ]; then echo "OK: $args"; else echo "FAIL: $args"; fi
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/cmp/cmp.sh; cp /workspace/executable /workspace/executable.mine 2>/dev/null; cd /workspace && git stash -q 2>/dev/null; cp executable /workspace/executable.ref 2>/dev/null || true; git stash pop -q 2>/dev/null; ls -la /workspace/executable*"}
output.name: bash
